title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Recording the Reactivation of a Dormant Account
content:
A dormant Savings & Money Market Accounts product returns to active status when its owner, identity verified, carries out a transaction of their own during the same contact, and that transaction's posting date becomes the account's new latest-activity date. This page is the entry point for recording such a reactivation where the owner's transaction is a transfer out to one of their own Personal Checking accounts.

## Scope

- **Covered.** Reactivation of a dormant savings or money market account through a transfer out that the owner makes during the contact, by telephone banking, online banking or the mobile app, into one of the owner's own checking accounts.
- **Not covered.** Reactivation through any other kind of transaction initiated by the owner.
- **Result governed.** The reactivation date to be recorded, which becomes the account's latest-activity date.

## Recording the reactivation

This is an agent action. Unlock `reactivate_savings_account_bfe70db1` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, then call it through `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Capability.** A single call moves the account's status to active and stores the date supplied as the date of the latest activity initiated by the customer, which is the date from which inactivity is measured again. Afterwards the account lookup shows the active status and the stored date.

## Parameters

- `savings_account_id`: identifier of the dormant savings or money market account, taken from the savings account lookup.
- `customer_id`: customer reference of the account owner whose identity was verified in this conversation, taken from the customer profile lookup.
- `reactivation_date`: the posted date of the customer-initiated transaction that brings the account back to active, written `YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Receipt

The call answers with a dictionary rendered as text holding `savings_account_id`, `customer_id`, `status` (always `active`) and `last_customer_activity_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the date stored). A status of active signals that the reactivation is on record.

## Quick answers

**Does the tool look at the ledger to find the date?** No. It stores whatever date it is given; the date itself comes from the policy's own rules applied to the account's records.

**Can this policy reactivate an account on the strength of a cash deposit at a branch?** No. That is a transaction of another kind and lies outside this policy.
